column2: How do I note where a collection is (archive service, fonds, reference) and who can see it?
column3: In a collection: “Edit” → “🏛 Where it is, who can see it”. Choose the archive service from the list in Settings → Archive services (or create it), write the fonds, the series, the reference, the collection’s online link, and the link to an image with {n} in place of the number (“…/vue/{n}”) plus the offset “Image = page + …”: each page then has “↗ Image 23 online” and “⧉ Cite this page” (“AD Cher, 3 E 1234, f° 11 r° (image 23)”). “Other copy” links the municipal copy and the court registry copy. Public access is calculated from the years and record types (75 years for births, marriages and notaries, immediately for deaths) or chosen (open, restricted until…, by permission): the app suggests, the archive service has the final say. In view-only mode, a collection not open to the public is hidden (switch in the “🔐 Who can see it” block). Also note the reuse (licence), the medium, the physical condition, the language, the handwriting and the provenance. On an archive service’s page: “📚 Collections held there”, their progress and their gaps.

column2: How do I see all my collections at a glance, by archive service and by fonds?
column3: Lists → 📚 Collections → “🏛 By fonds” (at the top, next to “📚 Collections”): the collections sorted by archive service then by fonds, and, within a fonds, by reference. At the top, the overall figures: collections, expected pages, photographed, transcribed, checked, absent pages and gaps. One row per collection: reference, dates, pages, photographed, transcribed · checked, online, open to the public, and what’s left (“2 to transcribe · 1 absent”); clicking “Remaining” opens the collection status. Each service and each fonds collapses (▸ ▾). “Show” keeps only what’s still to transcribe or proofread, and collections with absent pages, not online or not open to the public. “☰ Columns…” adds the series, medium, physical condition, language, reuse and numbering. “⤓ Spreadsheet” and “🖨 Holdings report” to send or print it. On the dashboard, the “🗂 Registers: still to do” widget shows the collections with the most left.

column2: What does a collection’s “💡 What’s in it” show, and what is the “Archive centre” profile for?
column3: In a collection’s summary, the “💡 What’s in it” block is calculated from the records already transcribed in the Workshop: records per year (years without records are hatched), record types, people mentioned (and how many are linked to a person record), the most frequent surnames, occupations (from the templates), places, the share of people who sign, the years covered. It adds remarks to check, never stated as fact: a year without records in the middle (“Mark a gap” adds it to Archive gaps) or a year with at least twice as many deaths as usual. The same block, for all the collections of a service, is on the archive service’s page. Lists → 📚 Collections → ⚙️ “Collection settings”: the “My family tree” profile (recommended) or “Archive centre, society” (the fonds view first, the medium, physical condition, language and reuse columns, and the identity card at the top of new collections’ summary), and the options: flag numbering gaps, show reliability, show remarks, hide collections not open to the public in view-only mode.
